title: Observational study: A quantitative analysis of anatomical parameters using ophthalmic imaging techniques to survey a healthy control cohort
summary:
Hannover Medical School is currently conducting a study to investigate the influence of immunoadsorption treatment (removal of antibodies (= antibodies) by a type of blood washing) on chronic fatigue (tiredness, fatigue) after COVID-19 infection. This study is funded by the Lower Saxony Ministry of Science and Culture and the COVID-19 Research Network Lower Saxony (COFONI). Participants in the EXTINCT study will take part in a non-invasive ophthalmologic examination (optical coherence tomography angiography), which is used to assess blood flow in the smallest vessels at the back of the eye. The reason for this is that previous studies have shown a connection between chronic fatigue and fine vascular changes in the retina and optic nerve.
In order to interpret the measurements of the patients from the EXTINCT study and to gain scientifically sound findings for future treatment and diagnostics, a comparison with healthy subjects is necessary. 

The first step is to determine visual acuity (visual acuity) using an autorefractometer. With this device, the spectacle values are automatically calculated using infrared light and an eye test with letters and numbers is then carried out. 
In optical coherence tomography (OCT), the retina is scanned with a weak laser light. The reflections of the light signals on the various retinal structures are measured and converted into image information by a computer system. With a layer analysis using SD-OCT, the optic nerve measurements and all retinal layers are segmented and displayed. The length of the eyeball is also measured using OCT technology. In addition, the images are qualitatively assessed and any morphological changes are documented.
A further module of the SPECTRALIS SD-OCT enables so-called OCT angiography (OCT-A) as a non-invasive diagnostic method for differentiated imaging of the retinal vessels and, to a lesser extent, the choroidal vessels. The laser scans the back of the eye without contact. 
The total duration of all examinations takes around 30-45 minutes. The examinations do not involve any additional risks and do not cause any changes to the eye.  All data is evaluated and published anonymously so that no conclusions can be drawn about the individual.

interventions.name: The study population consists of healthy volunteers who are recruited within the ophthalmic polyclinic of the medical school, public events or among the acquaintances of the study leaders. The inclusion is matched to the patient collective of the EXTINCT study (Extracorporeal apheresis Hannover Medi

Patient collective of the EXTINCT/COFONI study (Extracorporeal apheresis Hannover Medical school study in post-COVID patients). The examination of these patients is not part of this study. The age and gender distribution is used to create the study population (matching).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age- and sex-matched to the patient collective of the EXTINCT study
Exclusion criteria:
- Inadequate image quality due to insufficient light transmission of the optical media (cornea, lens, vitreous body) or lack of cooperation
- Pre-existing ophthalmological diseases
- Diabetes mellitus
- Chronic fatigue syndrome
- Lack of capacity to consent
- Previous apheresis therapy
- Additional oxygen requirement or ventilation during COVID infection
- Acute infectious diseases
- Pre-existing cardiovascular disease (e.g. arterial hypertension, vascular occlusion)
